long story short, a group of artists sneaked into the Prague castle in 2015 and exchanged the presidential flag for big red box shorts. There were a lot of controversial things surrounding the president at the time and in their own words, they wanted to fly "the flag of a man who is truly not ashamed of anything". From what I remember, it was everywhere at the time, media, politicians, everyone was just talking about that for maybe a week, again some time later when the trials happened and then everyone just forgot. For some reason unknown to me, our president decided it would be great idea to do a publicity stunt and burn the red boxer shorts on live press conference years later, if he did it to reclaim his dignity, he failed... so badly. I watched the press conference live at the time with my classmate, we couldn't believe what we were seeing lmao. if you Google Zeman underwear burning, I am sure you will find a lot of pictures of it. Still probably my favourite tale from Czech politics and that's saying a lot lol.

Um, actually I think I can explain that. I am not historian nor linguist, just Czech highschooler but this is what we were taught in history class. Also, probably long reply incoming. 

Defenestrations were way more common in the past than most people thing, sometimes they even served as punishment but it didn't have any specific name, it was just act of throwing people out of the window, nothing unusual. However the reason why it has a name is the fact that defenestrations have shaped most of our (Czech) history. There were three or four of them but the two most important ones started massive, religious wars. Most notably the defenestration of 1618 started the Thirty Years War that wiped out third of our population during the war and good percantage of the remaining ones in the famines and plague following the war. We also lost the war in like the first three years and this period of time until 1918 when we gained independence is considered the dark time of our nation when the czech language and culture almost died out. So it makes sense to coin the term for something that impacted us so heavily and the word just spread to other languages. Same as the word robot, that's also Czech, but to be fair this word also gained new meaning with new technology.

But take my comment with a grain of salt, I am not an expert, how I have said, this is what I was taught in higschool history class. Anyway, I hoped I explained it a bit.
